Funding Texts: Shafiq et al. [10] proposed CorrAUC by employing the following algorithms are used to detect malicious Bot-IoT traffic: Decision Tree (C4.5), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes (NB), and Random Forest (RF). CorrAUC is a new feature selection method that is based on a wrapper strategy for precisely filtering data and picking the best features for a selection of Machine Learning (ML) algorithm using Area Under Curve. CorrAUC was first introduced as a unique feature selection metric approach (AUC). Then, using an acceptable soft set as a foundation, integrated TOPSIS and Shannon Entropy were used to validate the chosen characteristics for identifying fraudulent traffic in an IoT network. Four distinct ML algorithms and the Bot-IoT database are used to evaluate the recommended technique. As a result, the recommended approach is supported by empirical assessment that provides, on average, successful results.
